Even though my supervisor keeps telling me it’s just routine feedback, it is very hard to shake the belief that there is a coordinated effort or some secret investigation going on at work and the hospital.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if these feelings of being evaluated and the hidden hints you perceive are interfering with your daily life and relationships, or are they more of a background worry that you can somewhat separate from your daily functioning?\n\nPatient: These thoughts are highly disruptive and definitely not just background worries. They make me incredibly anxious and distracted at work, which has led to me missing deadlines, getting written up, and having my clients reassigned. It doesn't feel like it's just a byproduct of my low mood; those hidden hints feel like an actual, troubling reality that I can't easily shake off.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situation that could potentially prove or disprove the idea that you're being secretly evaluated or that these hidden hints are real, or do you feel that this is something you just have to accept as true?\n\nPatient: On one hand, my supervisor keeps telling me that the feedback and delays are just routine paperwork, which logically suggests nothing secret is actually happening. But on the other hand, the feeling of people dropping hints in emails and meetings is so strong and persistent that it feels completely real to me. It leaves me feeling really stuck because I honestly don't know how I could ever prove or disprove it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think these feelings of being evaluated and the hidden hints are something that could potentially be influenced by your emotional state, or do they feel completely independent of how you're feeling emotionally?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure, and I haven't actually thought about whether there's a connection between the two. Even though I feel so emotionally blank and shut down, the hints and the feeling of being watched still feel incredibly real to me. It is just hard to say if my mood is influencing it or if they are completely separate things.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your mood were to significantly improve, these feelings of being secretly evaluated and the perception of hidden hints would also diminish, or would they likely remain as a distinct concern for you?"

These feelings and difficulties are entirely new to me, and they have just been building up over the past eight months. It is completely different from how I used to be.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this has been going on for about eight months and it's your first episode, but can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt somewhat better or back to normal during this time?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any periods where I felt better or back to my normal self. It has just been a continuous, steady decline with this constant heavy feeling since it all started. There hasn't been any break from it.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've experienced a steady decline over eight months without any periods of improvement, can you describe if there are any specific thoughts, feelings, or situations that you think might have triggered or significantly worsened this decline for you?\n\nPatient: It really started when my caseload at the community clinic became incredibly heavy, right around the same time my aging aunt in the Bronx needed more help with her medical issues. Juggling both of those heavy responsibilities just completely overwhelmed me, and that's when I felt myself start to shut down.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is your first episode and it's lasted about eight months without any periods of feeling back to normal, but can you tell me if you've had any periods in the past where you felt excessively happy, irritable, or had periods of high energy that might have lasted for a few days or more?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced anything like that. My mood and energy levels were always very stable and normal before these recent difficulties began. I've never had periods of excessive happiness, high energy, or irritability in the past.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant weight changes, changes in appetite, or alterations in your sleep pattern since the onset of these feelings, and if so, can you describe them?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any major changes in my weight, appetite, or sleep patterns. Honestly, those things haven't been my main focus because I've just been so consumed by this overall feeling of being shut down.\n\nDoctor: Given that this is your first episode and it has lasted for about eight months, do you think your symptoms would improve if the stressful situations, such as your heavy caseload and your aunt's health issues, were to resolve or significantly lessen?\n\nPatient: While those stressors definitely triggered and worsened my state, I'm really not sure if simply resolving them would fix how I feel now. This shut-down feeling and the blankness feel so deep and independent of external events. I honestly don't know if I could just snap back to normal even if my workload and caregiving duties disappeared.\n\nDoctor: You've had this continuous decline for eight months without feeling better, but looking back, do you think there was a specific point in time when your symptoms shifted from being just a reaction to stress to something more persistent and pervasive?\n\nPatient: The general shut-down feeling and lack of motivation definitely started building about eight months ago with the stress of work and my aunt's health. But a really distinct shift happened about two months ago when I started getting this unsettling feeling that people at work and the hospital were secretly evaluating me and dropping hidden hints. That felt completely different and much more intense than just normal stress.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being evaluated or receiving hidden hints from others, such as when they started, how often you experience them, and if they seem realistic to you now?\n\nPatient: They started about two months ago, and it feels like a coordinated effort at work and my aunt's hospital to secretly evaluate me, with people dropping hints in emails and staff meetings. My supervisor insists it's just routine feedback, but it feels incredibly real and unsettling to me. I'm just so exhausted that sometimes I feel really confused by it all.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling like people are secretly evaluating you and dropping hidden hints; do you think these perceptions are based on real events or might they be a product of your mind playing tricks on you?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor insists it's just routine feedback and paperwork delays, it feels incredibly real and convincing to me. It's really hard to shake the feeling that there is some kind of coordinated effort or secret evaluation going on, even when others try to reassure me otherwise.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other unusual experiences, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, aside from feeling like you're being secretly evaluated?\n\nPatient: No, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. But I have been having this strange experience where my coworkers tell me I'll suddenly freeze in the hallway or copy room, staring into space for several minutes. I don't even realize I'm doing it until someone touches my arm or calls my name to get me moving again.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the feelings of being evaluated or the hidden hints you perceive are definitely real, or could they possibly be a product of your own worries or stress?\n\nPatient: I know I am under an immense amount of stress right now, but these hints and feelings feel incredibly real to me. Even though my supervisor keeps telling me it’s just routine feedback, it is very hard to shake the belief that there is a coordinated effort or some secret investigation going on at work and the hospital.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if these feelings of being evaluated and the hidden hints you perceive are interfering with your daily life and relationships, or are they more of a background worry that you can somewhat separate from your daily functioning?\n\nPatient: These thoughts are highly disruptive and definitely not just background worries. They make me incredibly anxious and distracted at work, which has led to me missing deadlines, getting written up, and having my clients reassigned. It has also spilled over into my personal life, making me want to completely isolate myself at home and ignore calls from my friends because I just feel too overwhelmed and suspicious to connect with anyone.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if you weren't feeling so down and disconnected, these feelings of being evaluated and the hidden hints would still seem as real and disturbing to you, or are they closely tied to your overall mood and emotional state?\n\nPatient: While the emotional shutdown definitely makes everything harder to cope with, the feeling of being secretly investigated feels like a completely separate, very real issue. It doesn't feel like it's just a byproduct of my low mood; those hidden hints feel like an actual, troubling reality that I can't easily shake off.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situation that could potentially prove or disprove the idea that you're being secretly evaluated or that these hidden hints are real, or do you feel that this is something you just have to accept as true?\n\nPatient: On one hand, my supervisor keeps telling me that the feedback and delays are just routine paperwork, which logically suggests nothing secret is actually happening. But on the other hand, the feeling of people dropping hints in emails and meetings is so strong and persistent that it feels completely real to me. It leaves me feeling really stuck because I honestly don't know how I could ever prove or disprove it.\n\nDoctor: Do you think these feelings of being evaluated and the hidden hints are something that could potentially be influenced by your emotional state, or do they feel completely independent of how you're feeling emotionally?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure, and I haven't actually thought about whether there's a connection between the two. Even though I feel so emotionally blank and shut down, the hints and the feeling of being watched still feel incredibly real to me. It is just hard to say if my mood is influencing it or if they are completely separate things.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your mood were to significantly improve, these feelings of being secretly evaluated and the perception of hidden hints would also diminish, or would they likely remain as a distinct concern for you?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure because I haven't thought about whether my mood and those experiences are connected in that way. Even if I felt better emotionally, the feeling of being secretly evaluated feels so real and distinct to me right now. It doesn't seem like it's just a byproduct of me being tired or down.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that your feelings of being secretly evaluated would change if you were able to find evidence that clearly showed no one was watching or evaluating you, or would you still believe it was happening despite the evidence?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor has tried to reassure me that it’s just routine paperwork delays, I still can't shake the strong feeling that something else is going on. Honestly, even if someone showed me \"proof\" to the contrary, it would still feel incredibly real and hard to dismiss. I think I would just worry that they were covering it up or that the proof itself was somehow part of the test.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief in being secretly evaluated would change if multiple people, including those you trust, told you it wasn't true and showed you evidence to support that, or would you still hold onto the belief that it's happening?\n\nPatient: Even if people I deeply trust showed me evidence, I think I would still really struggle to let go of the belief. The feeling is just so intense and persistent that a strong part of me would still feel like the secret evaluation is happening. It feels so incredibly real that reassurance, even from them, wouldn't easily change my mind.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's a possibility that your feelings of being secretly evaluated could be a distortion of reality, rather than an actual fact, considering your overall emotional state and the significant stress you're under?\n\nPatient: I know I'm under an immense amount of stress right now with my work and caring for my aunt, but these feelings of being evaluated feel too specific and real to just be a distortion. Even though my supervisor insists it's all routine, the hints in emails and staff meetings feel so genuinely coordinated that I can't just dismiss it as stress.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would completely convince you that the secret evaluation is not happening, or do you feel that your belief in it is unshakeable regardless of any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: Despite my supervisor's reassurance that it's just routine feedback and paperwork delays, the patterns I see in emails and meetings feel far too deliberate and personal to ignore. Because of that, it is really hard for me to imagine what kind of evidence would actually convince me otherwise. The whole situation just feels too coordinated to be anything else.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your feelings of being secretly evaluated would still be present if you weren't experiencing the emotional shutdown and lack of motivation, or are these two issues closely linked in your mind?"

It doesn't feel like it's just a byproduct of my low mood; those hidden hints feel like an actual, troubling reality that I can't easily shake off.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any evidence or situation that could potentially prove or disprove the idea that you're being secretly evaluated or that these hidden hints are real, or do you feel that this is something you just have to accept as true?\n\nPatient: On one hand, my supervisor keeps telling me that the feedback and delays are just routine paperwork, which logically suggests nothing secret is actually happening. There hasn't been any break from it.\n\nDoctor: Given that you've experienced a steady decline over eight months without any periods of improvement, can you describe if there are any specific thoughts, feelings, or situations that you think might have triggered or significantly worsened this decline for you?\n\nPatient: It really started when my caseload at the community clinic became incredibly heavy, right around the same time my aging aunt in the Bronx needed more help with her medical issues. Juggling both of those heavy responsibilities just completely overwhelmed me, and that's when I felt myself start to shut down.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is your first episode and it's lasted about eight months without any periods of feeling back to normal, but can you tell me if you've had any periods in the past where you felt excessively happy, irritable, or had periods of high energy that might have lasted for a few days or more?\n\nPatient: No, I've never experienced anything like that. My mood and energy levels were always very stable and normal before these recent difficulties began. I've never had periods of excessive happiness, high energy, or irritability in the past.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant weight changes, changes in appetite, or alterations in your sleep pattern since the onset of these feelings, and if so, can you describe them?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any major changes in my weight, appetite, or sleep patterns. Honestly, those things haven't been my main focus because I've just been so consumed by this overall feeling of being shut down.\n\nDoctor: Given that this is your first episode and it has lasted for about eight months, do you think your symptoms would improve if the stressful situations, such as your heavy caseload and your aunt's health issues, were to resolve or significantly lessen?\n\nPatient: While those stressors definitely triggered and worsened my state, I'm really not sure if simply resolving them would fix how I feel now. This shut-down feeling and the blankness feel so deep and independent of external events. I honestly don't know if I could just snap back to normal even if my workload and caregiving duties disappeared.\n\nDoctor: You've had this continuous decline for eight months without feeling better, but looking back, do you think there was a specific point in time when your symptoms shifted from being just a reaction to stress to something more persistent and pervasive?\n\nPatient: The general shut-down feeling and lack of motivation definitely started building about eight months ago with the stress of work and my aunt's health. But a really distinct shift happened about two months ago when I started getting this unsettling feeling that people at work and the hospital were secretly evaluating me and dropping hidden hints. That felt completely different and much more intense than just normal stress.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being evaluated or receiving hidden hints from others, such as when they started, how often you experience them, and if they seem realistic to you now?\n\nPatient: They started about two months ago, and it feels like a coordinated effort at work and my aunt's hospital to secretly evaluate me, with people dropping hints in emails and staff meetings. My supervisor insists it's just routine feedback, but it feels incredibly real and unsettling to me. I'm just so exhausted that sometimes I feel really confused by it all.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling like people are secretly evaluating you and dropping hidden hints; do you think these perceptions are based on real events or might they be a product of your mind playing tricks on you?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor insists it's just routine feedback and paperwork delays, it feels incredibly real and convincing to me. Even though I feel so emotionally blank and shut down, the hints and the feeling of being watched still feel incredibly real to me. Even if I felt better emotionally, the feeling of being secretly evaluated feels so real and distinct to me right now. It doesn't seem like it's just a byproduct of me being tired or down.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that your feelings of being secretly evaluated would change if you were able to find evidence that clearly showed no one was watching or evaluating you, or would you still believe it was happening despite the evidence?\n\nPatient: Even though my supervisor has tried to reassure me that it’s just routine paperwork delays, I still can't shake the strong feeling that something else is going on. The feeling is just so intense and persistent that a strong part of me would still feel like the secret evaluation is happening. It feels so incredibly real that reassurance, even from them, wouldn't easily change my mind.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's a possibility that your feelings of being secretly evaluated could be a distortion of reality, rather than an actual fact, considering your overall emotional state and the significant stress you're under?\n\nPatient: I know I'm under an immense amount of stress right now with my work and caring for my aunt, but these feelings of being evaluated feel too specific and real to just be a distortion. Even though my supervisor insists it's all routine, the hints in emails and staff meetings feel so genuinely coordinated that I can't just dismiss it as stress.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that would completely convince you that the secret evaluation is not happening, or do you feel that your belief in it is unshakeable regardless of any evidence to the contrary?\n\nPatient: Despite my supervisor's reassurance that it's just routine feedback and paperwork delays, the patterns I see in emails and meetings feel far too deliberate and personal to ignore.
